history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2360 duplicates existing record seq 1083 (id kailash-temple-agra) — same temple, the Kailash Mandir at Sikandra on the Yamuna bank (CSV town 'Agra' is approximate; actual locality is Sikandra, about 8-12 km from central Agra). Identity confirmed: it is the only temple in Agra with twin shivlings together, one of the four Shiva temples at the city's corners; legend says Parashurama and Rishi Jamadagni received one shivling each from Shiva on Mount Kailash, and the lingams rooted immovably to the earth overnight at this spot. The annual Kailash Fair (August-September) is its main festival. Dedup decision needed — this record adds nothing new.

name: Kailash Temple, Agra
town_description: Agra, on the banks of the Yamuna in western Uttar Pradesh, was the capital of the Mughal Empire under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, and is home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri. Sikandra is a northwestern locality of Agra on NH-19 (Mathura Road), known for Akbar's tomb and the Kailash Mandir on the Yamuna bank.

travel.airport: Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyay Airport, Agra (Kheria).
travel.railway: Agra Cantt / Agra Fort railway stations.
travel.road: Sikandra on NH-19 (Mathura Road), on the Yamuna bank; about 8 km from Agra city centre.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Kailash Fair month (August-September) is the most festive.
visitor_information.opening_hours: See original record (seq 1083): 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM daily (a place listing gives 5:00 AM - 10:00 PM — verify).
